rationale: This is a small (1178 lines, 30 functions) dense numeric kernel — Jacobi eigenvalue iteration, QR factorization, and triangularization — dominated by a few large, hot, loop-heavy functions (Trianglelise, Jacobi, QRiterate, DivideAndSolve) where runtime overhead concentrates, so the cheapest low-risk transforms are weighted toward the security/diversity dimensions with low cost-dimension weights (SUB, SPLIT) so they fire broadly across all functions, while the expensive structural transforms get high cost-dimension weights (FLA, BCF) so they are selectively applied only to functions whose features justify the slowdown, protecting the big routines' control flow without crushing the hot loops; IBR gets moderate weighting as a good middle ground for branch obfuscation in the large functions, ICALL is kept modest because this benchmark has few call sites and indirect calls add per-call cost in tight numeric loops with some correctness exposure, and IGV is moderately favored since McCat-style code carries global state (matrix dimensions, print buffers) whose indirection raises analysis effort at low cost; correctness risk weights are kept low for the arithmetic-local passes (SUB, SPLIT, BCF) and higher only for the control-structure rewrites (FLA, ICALL) where miscompilation risk actually lives.
